object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: An individual in the system identified by a unique person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person employed by the organization, identified the same way as a person.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities for managing a department.

source_references.excerpt: Managers. A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit identified by a department code, with a unique department name.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code. Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

object_types.name: DepartmentName

ambiguities.description: Department management: Can multiple managers manage the same department? The transcript states 'A manager manages at most one department' but does not specify uniqueness on the Department side. Is each department managed by at most one manager, or could multiple managers share responsibility for a single department?

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department.

ambiguities.description: Department management mandatory participation: The transcript states 'Some managers are between assignments and manage none,' clarifying that managers need not manage any department. However, it is unclear whether every department must have a managing manager, or whether a department can exist without a manager.

source_references.excerpt: Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Employee-Manager overlap with department: The model includes both 'Employee works in Department' and 'Manager manages Department'. A manager is a subtype of employee, so every manager is also an employee. This raises the question: when a manager manages a department, must that manager also work in (be employed by) that same department, or can a manager manage a department different from their employing department?

ambiguities.description: Department name as alternate identifier: The transcript states 'no two share a name', indicating department names are unique. However, it is unclear whether department name is intended as an alternate (secondary) identifier alongside the primary department code, or merely a business rule that names happen to be unique without serving as an identifier.
